name: mkdir
plain: `mkdir` creates a new folder. With -p it creates the whole chain (parents too) and does not complain if the folder already exists.
when: Start a new project or working folder.
Create a nested path in one go.
Create a directory with specific permissions.

examples.title: Make a folder
examples.explain: Creates loot in the current directory.

examples.title: Make a nested path
examples.explain: -p creates ctf, ctf/web and ctf/web/notes, whichever are missing, and is happy if they exist.

examples.title: Brace expansion for a tree
examples.explain: The shell expands the braces into four paths, so one command creates a whole layout.

examples.title: Set permissions at creation
examples.explain: -m sets the mode: 700 means only you can enter.

examples.title: Show what is created
examples.explain: -v prints a line for every directory created.

options.plain: Make parent directories as needed; no error if existing.
Print a message for each created directory.

mistakes: Forgetting -p and getting 'No such file or directory'.
Spaces in names: mkdir my folder makes two folders.
Creating a folder that needs root (like in /opt) without sudo.
try: Build a CTF folder tree with one command using braces.
Make a private folder with -m 700 and check it with ls -ld.
Run mkdir -p twice and see that the second run is silent.
see_also: rmdir(1), cp(1), mv(1), ls(1), chmod(1), install(1), touch(1).
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
